title: Arrest struggle leads to man's death
article: A man is dead and a Westside RCMP officer seriously injured with possible broken bones after an early morning struggle in a Westbank neighbourhood Wednesday.
Police said the man, who was originally involved in a violent domestic dispute with his parents, seemed to possess "super-human" strength when he took on the officers.
"These officers were very large officers and physically capable," said RCMP operations support officer Insp. Steve McVarnock.
"For them to go through this is something out of the ordinary."
McVarnock said it eventually took five officers to finally subdue 38-year-old Derrick Patrick Madrusan, six-feet tall and about 160 pounds.
Madrusan seemed to have his way with the first two, then another officer was called out and finally two more. None were trained or equipped in using a taser, he said, so one wasn't used.

They bound Madrusan's hands behind his back and used bracelets on his legs, then placed him in a police cruiser. McVarnock couldn't say if Madrusan was conscious at that time, but he was placed in the recovery position as per procedure.
He was left alone there for "moments," McVarnock said.
When another officer went to check on him, they found him unresponsive.
Ambulance paramedics moved from working on the man's parents, who are each in their 70s, to Madrusan. He was declared dead upon arrival at hospital.
A neighbour to the four-plex where Madrusan recently lived with his parents, said this wasn't the first commotion the junior Madrusan had caused.
Frank VanKasteen witnessed much of the confrontation but refused to say if, in his opinion, police used excessive force.
"I was a police officer in the Netherlands for 15 years," he said. "I don't like that question."
A team of RCMP major crimes investigators were combing the scene Wednesday morning.
McVarnock said they are just one layer of accountability over the incident.
An internal review is underway and the B.C. Coroner's Service is duty-bound to investigate in-custody deaths.
Officially, McVarnock said Madrusan died of "unknown injuries as a result of an altercation with police."
An autopsy will determine what role, if any, drugs may have played.
Madrusan has a lengthy criminal record dating back to 1986, mostly for property offences and one assault.
None of his charges since 1997 were for drugs.
He was sentenced to five years in prison in March for robbery in Vancouver Supreme Court. It's unclear why he was still at large. He was required to report regularly to authorities.
But while police had plenty of information about Madrusan, they refused to release names of the officers involved and their service records.
"I want to assure the community that RCMP members on scene during this incident are very distraught over this situation," McVarnock said.

"This encounter was a very volatile situation with an extremely agitated male subject and our members were at extreme risk while trying to subdue the deceased prior to his passing. We stand behind our members..."
He said at least one officer suffered multiple injuries and possible broken bones . The officer is currently recovering at home.
